title: Exact geometric stalks and the constant-complex retraction
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. On the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] let $A_T$ be the constant ring sheaf and $c(M)=\underline M$ the constant $A_T$-module sheaf of an ordinary $A$-module $M$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Write $S(F)=F_{\bar t}$ for the geometric stalk with its induced $A$-module action [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Use sheaves of modules over $A_T$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and apply $S$ and $c$ termwise to unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C$ be any such complex of $A_T$-module sheaves and $E$ any such complex of ordinary $A$-modules. Both are exact additive functors on their respective abelian categories, and there are natural $A$-linear cohomology isomorphisms
$$H^n(SC)\cong S(H^n(C)),\qquad H^n(cE)\cong c(H^n(E))\quad(n\in\mathbf Z).$$
Consequently each termwise functor preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. There is a natural chain isomorphism $\eta_E:E\xrightarrow{\sim}S(cE)$ whose degree-$n$ component sends $e\in E^n$ to the germ at $(T,\bar t)$ of its constant section. In particular $S(A_T)\cong A$ has the ordinary scalar action. All assertions hold for arbitrary unbounded complexes, without any finiteness hypothesis on $A$.

proof.text: The constant-presheaf functor takes a short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ of ordinary $A$-modules to a sectionwise short exact sequence of presheaves: at every object it is the given sequence, with identity restriction maps. Regard the constant presheaf $U\mapsto M$ as a presheaf of modules over the constant presheaf of rings $U\mapsto A$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], applied with $\mathcal O$ that constant ring presheaf (whose ring sheafification is $A_T$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]), its sheafification $c(M)$ is a sheaf of $A_T$-modules, functorial in $M$ for $A$-linear maps, the canonical map from the constant presheaf to $c(M)$ is linear over $A\to A_T$, and the underlying abelian sheaf of $c(M)$ is the abelian sheafification of the constant presheaf $U\mapsto M$, with the same canonical map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact](1),(2) with $R=\mathbf Z$: abelian sheafification is exact, so the underlying abelian sheaves of $c(M')\to c(M)\to c(M'')$ form a short exact sequence. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1) the forgetful functor $\mathrm{Mod}(A_T)\to\mathrm{Ab}(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels; hence it preserves the homology objects of a composable pair, and a faithful additive functor sends only zero objects to zero (if $F(X)=0$ then $F(\mathrm{id}_X)=0=F(0)$). So it reflects short exactness, and $c(M')\to c(M)\to c(M'')$ is short exact in $\mathrm{Mod}(A_T)$. Thus $c$ is exact; it is additive because the map induced by $f+g$ is the sum of those induced by $f,g$ on the constant presheaves and sheafification is additive. This uses arbitrary $A$-modules, not the finite-module constant-exactness lemma.

source.place: Tag 03EI, label lemma-sheafification-exact (PMod(O) to Mod(O^#) for the constant presheaf of rings O=A); reflection through the forgetful functor, Tag 03DA, label lemma-abelian

proof.text: For an $A$-module $M$, step 1 identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $c(M)$ with the abelian constant sheaf $\underline M$, the canonical maps $\iota_U$ agreeing. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] to it. It gives the bijective additive map $\eta_M:M\to S(cM)$ sending $m$ to the germ of $\iota_T(m)$ at $(T,\bar t)$. The scalar action of $a\in A$ on a germ of $s\in F(U)$ is the germ of $\iota_U(a)s$; this is well defined because restriction is semilinear [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\iota$ commutes with restriction. By the linearity of the canonical map over $A\to A_T$ in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], $\iota_T(a)\iota_T(m)=\iota_T(am)$ and $\iota_T(a)\iota_T(b)=\iota_T(ab)$, $\iota_T(1)=1$. Hence $\eta_A(1)=1$, $\eta_A(ab)=\eta_A(a)\eta_A(b)$ and $\eta_M(am)=a\cdot\eta_M(m)=\eta_A(a)\eta_M(m)$. So $\eta_A:A\cong S(A_T)$ is a ring isomorphism, $\eta_M$ is $A$-linear for the specified scalar action, and for each linear $f:M\to N$ the sheaf map $c(f)$ sends $\iota_T(m)$ to $\iota_T(f(m))$, so $S(cf)\eta_M(m)=\eta_N(f(m))$. This proves naturality in ordinary modules. Germs of a sum of sheaf morphisms are sums of their germs, so $S$ is additive as well.

source.place: Tag 03PT, label lemma-stalk-exact, clause (2); constant-germ normalization; sites-modules.tex, stalk operations immediately before Tag 04EQ

proof.text: Given a short exact sequence of $A_T$-module sheaves, forgetting scalars leaves a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1). Applying [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives a short exact sequence of underlying abelian groups. Its maps are $A$-linear for the action fixed in step 2. For linear maps the kernel and image as sets are the same subgroups and submodules, and surjectivity is independent of forgetting scalars. Thus this sequence is short exact as ordinary $A$-modules, proving exactness of $S$.

source.place: Tag 04EQ, label lemma-stalk-exact-modules, clause (1), reducing to abelian exactness using Tag 03DA, label lemma-abelian

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] first to $S$ and $C$, and then to $c$ and $E$. Its hypotheses are the additive exactness established in steps 1 and 3: an additive functor of abelian categories carrying short exact sequences to short exact sequences preserves kernels and cokernels (apply it to $0\to\ker f\to X\to\operatorname{im}f\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}f\to Y\to\operatorname{coker}f\to0$, Stacks Tag 010N, homology.tex lemma-exact-functor), and with finite biproducts hence all finite limits and colimits. It identifies the kernels of the mapped differentials and the images of the preceding mapped differentials with the images under the functor of the original cycles and boundaries; passing to their quotient gives $H^n(SC)\cong S(H^n(C))$ and $H^n(cE)\cong c(H^n(E))$. The cited statement gives naturality in complex maps and compatibility with cycles and the cohomology projections. These are isomorphisms in the respective module categories, so the first is $A$-linear and the second is $A_T$-linear.

source.place: Tag 010N, label lemma-exact-functor, applied degreewise to cycles and boundaries

proof.text: Both functors send zero objects to zero objects. The isomorphisms of step 4 therefore send a complex with all cohomology zero to one with all cohomology zero. For a quasi-isomorphism $f$, naturality gives $H^n(Ff)=(c^n_{\mathrm{target}})^{-1}F(H^n(f))c^n_{\mathrm{source}}$ for $F=S$ or $F=c$; all three factors are invertible. Thus both termwise functors preserve acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. The argument in a fixed degree uses only the two adjacent differentials and their kernel/image quotient, and applies to every integer degree without bounds.

source.place: Tag 010N, label lemma-exact-functor; degreewise consequence of the cohomology comparisons

proof.text: Set $(\eta_E)^n=\eta_{E^n}$ from step 2. Naturality there applied to $d_E^n:E^n\to E^{n+1}$ says $S(c(d_E^n))\eta_{E^n}=\eta_{E^{n+1}}d_E^n$, precisely the chain-map equation. Each component is an isomorphism, and the same equation multiplied by the component inverses proves that the inverse family is a chain map. For a complex map $u:E\to E^{\prime}$, the degreewise identity $S(c(u^n))\eta_{E^n}=\eta_{E^{\prime n}}u^n$ proves naturality of the chain isomorphism. Its components have the prescribed constant-germ formula; step 2 with $M=A$ gives the ordinary scalar action. No step used finiteness of $A$ or a bound on $E$ or $C$.
